Consumer Non-Cyclicals: Consumer Non-Cyclicals posted a robust average annual earnings growth of 35.54%, placing the sector ninth out of fifteen sectors for earnings expansion, while its average annual revenue grew 11.98%, earning a sixth place ranking for revenue growth. The strong earnings pace was led by [#VC2.SI]Olam Group Ltd[\#VC2.SI], which recorded the highest yearly earnings increase in the sector, and [#EB5.SI]First Resources Ltd[\#EB5.SI] delivered the top revenue growth. Growth was further supported by Singapore’s high per‑capita consumption of essential goods, a stable regulatory environment for food and beverage retailers, and continued government initiatives to boost local food security, all of which uniquely benefit non‑cyclical consumer firms. These sector‑specific dynamics helped sustain the impressive earnings and revenue gains despite broader market volatility.
Consumer Cyclicals: The Consumer Cyclicals sector posted an average annual earnings decline of 4.39% while its revenue grew by 14.82% over the past year. Among fifteen SGX sectors, it ranked 13th for earnings growth and 3rd for revenue growth. [#51O.SI]MSM International Ltd[\#51O.SI] delivered the strongest earnings expansion in the sector, and [#5OX.SI]Mary Chia Holdings Ltd[\#5OX.SI] achieved the highest revenue increase. The sector’s performance is shaped by Singapore’s recent rebound in tourism, which lifted demand for retail and leisure services, and by robust festive spending that boosted consumer discretionary purchases. In addition, the easing of vehicle import restrictions and rising household savings have supported automotive and home‑goods sales, helping revenue to rise even as earnings faced pressure.
Transportation & Logistics: The Transportation & Logistics sector posted modest earnings growth of 1.75% over the past year, placing it twelfth out of fifteen sectors for earnings expansion. Revenue rose by 2.7%, which ranks the sector thirteenth among its peers for top-line growth. Within the sector, [#FQ7.SI]Salt Investments Ltd[\#FQ7.SI] recorded the strongest earnings increase, while [#R14.SI]Eneco Energy Ltd[\#R14.SI] delivered the highest revenue growth. Growth in Singapore is shaped by the nation’s status as a regional transshipment hub, recent expansions at the port that temporarily limited capacity, government incentives for digital freight platforms, and tighter labour supply in warehousing and trucking that together influence both cost structures and service efficiency.
Healthcare: Despite a sharp contraction in earnings, the Healthcare sector posted an average annual earnings decline of about 74.6 percent, placing it second‑worst among the fifteen sectors, while its average annual revenue rose 13.2 percent, earning a mid‑range fifth‑best ranking. The sector’s earnings slump is reflected in the performance of [#FHH.SI]FHH[\#FHH.SI], which recorded the highest yearly earnings growth within the sector despite the overall downturn. On the revenue side, [#8YY.SI]Embracing Future Holdings Ltd[\#8YY.SI] led the sector with the strongest yearly revenue increase. Growth in Singapore’s healthcare market is further shaped by the nation’s ageing population and the government’s expanding public health initiatives, which drive demand for medical services and long‑term care. At the same time, strict local regulatory pathways for new medical products can limit rapid earnings expansion for many companies.
Properties & Real Estate: Properties & Real Estate posted an average annual earnings growth of about 84.6% and a revenue increase of roughly 13.3% over the past year, ranking third in earnings growth and fourth in revenue growth among fifteen SGX sectors. The sector’s strong earnings surge is led by [#5IC.SI][#5IC.SI]SING Holdings Ltd[\#5IC.SI][\#5IC.SI], which recorded the highest yearly earnings growth, while the same company also delivered the top revenue growth within the group. Singapore’s limited land supply and tight zoning regulations continue to drive premium pricing and redevelopment activity, amplifying profit margins for well‑positioned developers. At the same time, recent cooling measures on residential loans and tighter foreign buyer restrictions temper demand, shaping a more selective revenue expansion. Together, these market‑specific dynamics explain why earnings have accelerated far more than revenue in this sector.
Energy: Energy sector posted robust growth, with average annual earnings rising about 21.7% and revenue climbing roughly 20.8% over the past year. This earnings expansion places the sector tenth among fifteen sectors, while its revenue performance ranks it first, highlighting a stronger top‑line momentum. The standout earnings performer is [#JFQ.SI]JFQ[\#JFQ.SI], which recorded the highest yearly earnings growth in the sector, and [#TPED.SI]PTT Exploration Production PCL DRC[\#TPED.SI] led revenue growth. Growth was further supported by Singapore’s role as a regional hub for oil trading and the recent expansion of LNG storage capacity, which amplified demand for energy services. Additionally, the sector benefited from government incentives aimed at diversifying energy sources, encouraging investment in offshore exploration and renewable integration, factors that are specific to the Singapore market.
Utilities: The Utilities sector posted a striking 47.76% average annual earnings growth, positioning it sixth among fifteen sectors for earnings expansion. Conversely, its average annual revenue fell 5.56%, the weakest performance, ranking it fifteenth for revenue growth. [#5GD.SI]Sunpower Group Ltd[\#5GD.SI] led the sector with the highest yearly earnings growth, while [#BEH.SI]China International Holdings Ltd[\#BEH.SI] recorded the strongest revenue increase. In Singapore, recent regulatory tariff adjustments and the accelerated shift toward renewable energy sources have boosted earnings potential but also compressed revenue as traditional consumption patterns evolve.
Consumer Defensive: The Consumer Defensive sector posted an impressive average annual earnings growth of 49.24%, ranking fifth among fifteen sectors. Its average annual revenue grew by 10.98%, placing the sector seventh in revenue growth. [#CNE.SI]MindChamps PreSchool Ltd[\#CNE.SI] delivered the highest yearly earnings growth within the sector, while [#5EG.SI]Zhongxin Fruit and Juice Ltd[\#5EG.SI] achieved the strongest yearly revenue growth. Growth has been bolstered by strong household demand for essential services such as early childhood education, which benefits from Singapore's emphasis on quality schooling, and by increasing consumer preference for locally produced, health‑focused fruit juices, both of which are unique drivers for this sector.
Financial Services: Over the past year the Financial Services sector posted an average annual earnings growth of 8.94% and an average annual revenue growth of 8.59%. In the SGX ranking the sector sits at 11th place for earnings growth and 9th place for revenue growth among fifteen sectors. [#I49.SI]IFS Capital Ltd[\#I49.SI] recorded the strongest earnings expansion in the sector, while [#K6S.SI]Prudential PLC[\#K6S.SI] delivered the highest revenue increase. Growth in Singapore’s financial services is further shaped by the Monetary Authority of Singapore’s ongoing push for fintech innovation, which encourages banks to adopt digital platforms and creates new fee‑based income streams. At the same time, the country’s high savings rate and steady demand for wealth‑management services support both earnings and revenue expansion. These sector‑specific dynamics help explain the solid but modestly ranked growth performance.
Communication Services: Despite a modest 3.12% rise in average annual revenue, the Communication Services sector posted a steep decline in earnings, with an average annual earnings contraction of 135.83%. This performance places the sector at the bottom of the earnings growth ranking, 15th out of 15 sectors, while its revenue growth ranking sits at 12th. The sector’s earnings weakness is amplified by Singapore’s stringent content licensing rules and the recent increase in spectrum fees, which have squeezed profit margins for broadcasters and telecom operators. At the same time, the rapid rollout of 5G infrastructure and strong consumer demand for streaming services have helped sustain a small positive revenue trend. Within the sector, [#9VW.SI][#9VW.SI]Spackman Entertainment Group Ltd[\#9VW.SI][\#9VW.SI] leads both earnings and revenue growth, recording the highest yearly increases among its peers.
Basic Materials: Over the past year the Basic Materials sector posted an extraordinary average earnings growth of about 1110.32%, placing it first among the fifteen SGX sectors. Its average revenue grew 9.36%, which ranks eighth in the same peer set. [#KUO.SI]International Cement Group Ltd[\#KUO.SI] delivered the strongest earnings surge within the sector, while [#C8R.SI]Jiutian Chemical Group Ltd[\#C8R.SI] led the revenue expansion. Growth has been amplified by Singapore’s ongoing large‑scale infrastructure upgrades that boost demand for cement and construction inputs, as well as tighter environmental standards that favor firms with efficient production processes. These sector‑specific dynamics, together with the standout performances of the two companies, underpin the robust earnings and moderate revenue gains observed.
Infrastructures: Despite modest revenue expansion, the Infrastructures sector posted an extraordinary earnings surge, with average annual earnings growth of about 338.28%, placing it second among fifteen sectors for earnings growth. Revenue grew only 1.81% on average, ranking the sector fourteenth for revenue expansion. [#Z74.SI]Singapore Telecommunications Ltd[\#Z74.SI] delivered the strongest earnings acceleration within the sector, while [#S59.SI]SIA Engineering Co Ltd[\#S59.SI] led revenue growth. The sector’s performance is shaped by Singapore’s limited land area, which drives continuous investment in utility networks and transport corridors, and by the government’s ongoing push to upgrade ports and airport facilities to sustain the city-state’s status as a logistics hub. These localized infrastructure upgrades and regulatory commitments underpin the divergent earnings and revenue trends observed.
REIT: Strong earnings momentum characterises Singapore’s REIT sector, with an average annual earnings growth of 39.3% that places the sector eighth among fifteen sectors. Revenue expansion is more modest, averaging 4.29% and ranking tenth in the same peer group. The sector’s performance is driven by factors unique to Singapore’s property market, such as a constrained supply of prime commercial space and sustained demand from both local and foreign investors seeking stable yields. In addition, the regulatory framework that encourages transparent distribution policies supports investor confidence in REITs. Within the sector, [#M1GU.SI]Alpha Integrated REIT[\#M1GU.SI] leads the pack in earnings growth, while [#DCRU.SI]Digital Core REIT[\#DCRU.SI] posts the highest revenue growth.
Industrials: Industrials posted a striking earnings surge, with an average annual earnings growth of 55.55%, placing the sector fourth among fifteen sectors for earnings expansion. Revenue, however, grew more modestly at an average annual rate of 3.18%, ranking the sector eleventh in revenue growth across the market. The strongest earnings performance came from [#5OC.SI]Koyo International Ltd[\#5OC.SI], which recorded the highest yearly earnings increase within the sector, while [#Y06.SI]Green Build Technology Ltd[\#Y06.SI] led the group in revenue growth. Growth in the Industrials sector is further supported by Singapore’s ongoing expansion of port facilities and the government’s emphasis on upgrading transport infrastructure, which create demand for heavy equipment and construction services. These sector-specific drivers help explain the pronounced earnings gains despite relatively slower revenue growth.
Technology: Technology sector posted an average annual earnings growth of about 45.7%, placing it seventh among fifteen sectors for earnings expansion. Its average annual revenue growth was roughly 15.9%, earning the second‑best rank for revenue growth. The strongest earnings increase came from [#BLU.SI]GRP Ltd[\#BLU.SI], while [#9MT.SI]MetaOptics Ltd[\#9MT.SI] led the sector in revenue growth. Growth was further fueled by Singapore’s aggressive smart‑nation roadmap, which drives corporate investment in cloud services and artificial intelligence. The nation’s generous R&D tax incentives and extensive 5G rollout also created a conducive environment for tech firms to scale. At the same time, a tight local talent pool pushes companies to adopt automation, adding to the earnings momentum.
